customdata:
{"name": "Sun", "subtitle": "", "body": "Note: The Sun, our very own star, is a massive ball of hot plasma that sits at the center of our solar system.
It's the source of all life and energy on Earth, so I've colored it chlorophyll green in our plot!
* Type: A yellow dwarf star (G-type main-sequence star).
* Age: About 4.6 billion years old, and is expected to continue its current phase for about 5 billion years
more, then evolve into a Red Giant.
* Diameter: Roughly 1.4 million kilometers (865,000 miles), about 109 times the diameter of Earth.
* Mass: About 333,000 times the mass of Earth
* Composition: Primarily hydrogen (about 73%) and helium (about 25%), with trace amounts of other elements.
* Surface Temperature: 5778 K, around 5,500 degrees Celsius, or 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit
* Core Temperature: Around 15 million degrees Celsius (27 million degrees Fahrenheit)
* Stellar Class: Main-sequence. Stars in the prime of their lives, fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores.
* Absolute Magnitude: 4.83
* Spectral Type: G2V
* Object Type: Star
The Sun is composed of several layers:
* Core: The innermost region where nuclear fusion occurs, converting hydrogen into helium and releasing energy.
* Radiative Zone: Energy from the core travels outward through this zone via radiation.
* Convective Zone: Energy is transported through this zone via convection (the movement of hot plasma).
* Photosphere: The visible surface of the Sun.
* Chromosphere: A thin layer above the photosphere.
* Corona: The outermost layer, a very hot and tenuous plasma that extends millions of kilometers into space.
Standard for comparison to other stars:
* Luminosity: 1.000000 Lsun
* Mass: 1.00 Msun
* Distance: 0 pc (0 ly)
* Plotting marker size: 12 px"}

It's the source of all life and energy on Earth, so I've colored it chlorophyll green in our plot!
* Type: A yellow dwarf star (G-type main-sequence star).
* Age: About 4.6 billion years old, and is expected to continue its current phase for about 5 billion years
more, then evolve into a Red Giant.
* Diameter: Roughly 1.4 million kilometers (865,000 miles), about 109 times the diameter of Earth.
* Mass: About 333,000 times the mass of Earth
* Composition: Primarily hydrogen (about 73%) and helium (about 25%), with trace amounts of other elements.
* Surface Temperature: 5778 K, around 5,500 degrees Celsius, or 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit
* Core Temperature: Around 15 million degrees Celsius (27 million degrees Fahrenheit)
* Stellar Class: Main-sequence. Stars in the prime of their lives, fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores.
* Absolute Magnitude: 4.83
* Spectral Type: G2V
* Object Type: Star
The Sun is composed of several layers:
* Core: The innermost region where nuclear fusion occurs, converting hydrogen into helium and releasing energy.
* Radiative Zone: Energy from the core travels outward through this zone via radiation.
* Convective Zone: Energy is transported through this zone via convection (the movement of hot plasma).
* Photosphere: The visible surface of the Sun.
* Chromosphere: A thin layer above the photosphere.
* Corona: The outermost layer, a very hot and tenuous plasma that extends millions of kilometers into space.

_encyclopedia.16 Psyche:
Horizons: 16 or 20000016 or A852 FA. Scientists hypothesize that Psyche might be the exposed core of a "planetesimal" 
—a building block of an early planet that had its rocky outer layers stripped away by violent collisions billions of years ago. 
16 Psyche is the target of the NASA Psyche mission. The spacecraft is expected to reach the asteroid in August 2029. 
16 Psyche is a unique, metal-rich asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Unlike most 
asteroids that are composed of rock or ice, Psyche appears to be made largely of nickel and iron—similar to the core of Earth.
_encyclopedia.Psyche:
Horizons:-255. JPL: "BACKGROUND:
Psyche is a NASA Discovery-class mission to map the surface and characterize
the composition of '16 Psyche', an elongated 280-km diameter metal-rich
asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. This
is the first mission to a metal-rich asteroid.

Psyche was launched Oct 13, 2023 @ 14:19:43 UTC on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy
from Kennedy Space Center, LC-39A.  Stage separation occurred 62 minutes
after launch at 15:21 UTC.

A gravity-assist flyby of Mars will occur in May 2026 at an altitude of
3000-4400 km above the surface, exact details depending on launch date.

The arrival phase ends June 26, 2029.
The asteroid's gravity will capture the spacecraft into orbit in late July
2029 and the two-year prime mission will begin in August. Psyche will
successively lower its orbit over the span of a year, eventually coming
as close as 75-km from the asteroid's surface.
_encyclopedia.Sun:
Horizons: 10. The star at the center of our solar system. To display structure and atmosphere select "Solar Shells".

* Missions:
  * Pioneer 5 (NASA/DOD, 1960): Measured magnetic field phenomena, solar flare particles, and ionization.
  * Helios 1 & 2 (DFVLR/NASA, 1974 & 1976): Studied solar wind, magnetic and electric fields, cosmic rays, and dust.
  * ISEE-3 (NASA, 1978): Observed solar phenomena in conjunction with Earth-orbiting satellites, comets.
  * Ulysses (ESA/NASA, 1990-2009): Observed the Sun's polar regions and the solar wind at high solar latitudes.
  * WIND (NASA, 1994-Present): Still active, it provides continuous measurements of the solar wind.
  * SOHO (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory) (ESA/NASA, 1995-Present): A continuous view from its core to the solar wind.
  * ACE (Advanced Composition Explorer) (NASA, 1997-Present): Measures particles from the solar wind and galactic cosmic rays.
  * Hinode (JAXA/NASA/ESA/STFC, 2006-Present): Explores the Sun's magnetic fields.
  * STEREO (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory) (NASA, 2006-Present): Imaging the 3D structure of coronal mass ejections.
  * Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) (NASA, 2010-Present): High-resolution images of solar flares and eruptions.
  * IRIS (Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph) (NASA, 2013-Present): Sun's lower atmosphere (chromosphere and transition).
  * Parker Solar Probe (NASA, 2018-Present): Flew through the corona to study coronal heating and solar wind acceleration.
  * Solar Orbiter (ESA/NASA, 2020-Present): Provides unprecedented insight into how our local star "works" with 10 science instruments.
  * PUNCH (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere) (NASA, Launched March 2025): Will study the Sun's outer atmosphere.
  * Solar Polar Orbit Observatory (Planned 2029): Will study views of its polar regions.
